# Synod diagnostic codes

Generated by `synod explain --catalog`; do not edit.

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntax` | The structure grammar cannot parse the line. | Write a digit before the point. |
| `indent` | The indentation of a line is wrong. | Indent each level by exactly 2 spaces. |
| `non-canonical` | The code can be read but is not written in canonical form. | Write the settings in the order the fields are declared, or let `synod fmt` do it. |
| `bad-header` | The file's package header is missing or wrong. | Name the package after its folder. |
| `unknown-phrase` | No phrase matches the sentence by its shape. | Parenthesize the condition. |
| `ambiguous-phrase` | More than one phrase matches the sentence by its shape. | Rename the phrase so its shape is its own. |
| `duplicate-name` | A name is defined twice in one namespace. | Give the second phrase another name. |
| `shadowing` | A name hides another name that is already in scope. | Rename the second name. |
| `reserved-word` | A reserved word is used as a name or a head. | Choose a name that is not a reserved word. |
| `bad-pattern` | A `define` or `when` pattern breaks the pattern rules. | Put a word between the two holes. |
| `bad-receiver` | A receiver is of the wrong type or in the wrong place. | Give the receiver the type `Node`. |
| `bad-place` | `set` targets something that cannot be set. | Set a local instead of the parameter. |
| `type-mismatch` | A value has a type that is not accepted where it is used. | Pass a value of the type the hole expects. |
| `ambiguous-empty` | The type of `{}` cannot be told. | Use the place with a `std/lists` or `std/maps` phrase, so the type is known. |
| `missing-result` | A value phrase has a path that does not reach `result`. | End every path with a `result`. |
| `value-as-statement` | A phrase that gives a value stands where a statement is expected. | Use the value. |
| `action-as-value` | A phrase that gives no value is used as a value. | Call the phrase as a statement. |
| `unexported` | A lower-case name from another package is used. | Export the phrase by giving it an upper-case head. |
| `unused-name` | A local or `each` name is never read. | Use the local, or remove it. |
| `unused-import` | An import is never used. | Remove the import. |
| `unneeded-alias` | `use … as` is written where there is no collision. | Remove the alias and use the last segment. |
| `unknown-import` | An import path does not name a library package. | Spell the path as the folder is named. |
| `import-cycle` | Packages import each other in a circle. | Break the cycle so that only one package imports the other. |
| `missing-main` | A main file has no `define main`, or `synod run` finds no main file. | Add the entry. |
| `extra-main` | A folder has more than one `define main`, or `define main` is in a library file. | Keep one `define main`. |
| `context` | A statement is not allowed in the context it runs in. | Write the setup in main with a phrase that takes the node as a hole. |
| `foreign-state` | Node code reaches another node's state. | Take the value as a hole. A real peer would send it in a message with `net.Send`. |
| `color-literal` | A color literal stands where only a named color is allowed. | Remove the holes, so the phrase names the color. |
| `native-outside-std` | `native` is used outside `std/`. | Write the body in Synod. |
| `theme-outside-main` | A library file imports a theme. | Remove the import: the main file of the program selects its theme. |
| `extra-theme` | A main file imports more than one theme. | Remove the second theme. |
| `bad-theme` | A theme file is not a complete theme. | Define every name of the theme table. |
| `missing-key` | A map was asked for a key it does not hold. | Set the key before reading it. |
| `index-range` | A list index is not a whole number from 0 up to one less than the size of the list. | Use an index below the size of the list, counting from 0. |
| `disk-type` | A value read from a node's disk does not have the type of the default given to `disk.Read`. | Write the same kind of value that the default has. |
| `division-by-zero` | A number or a time was divided by zero. | Divide by a number that is not zero. |
| `nobody` | `sim.Nobody` was used where a node is needed. | Name a real node, such as one made with `sim.Spawn`. |
| `time-limit` | The next event is later than 10 minutes of simulated time. | Keep every delay within 10 minutes. |
| `bad-argument` | An argument is outside the domain of the phrase that received it. | Pass a value inside the domain, here a delay of 0 or more. |
| `number-range` | A calculation gave a number that is not finite, or a time that does not fit in 64 bits. | Keep the calculation within the range of the type. |
| `run-limit` | The run exceeded one of the limits that keep a program from running forever. | Let the call end, here by taking a count that runs out. |
